title: Two seas
hookLine: two seas meet with a barrier between them they don't cross (55:19–20)

lines: A MUDDY RIVER, A CLEAR SEA.
cards: Stand on a bridge where a muddy river runs into clear water, and sometimes you can see the line: brown on one side, blue-green on the other, running side by side before they blend.
Pour cream into cold coffee without stirring and you get a small version on the kitchen table. Two things touching, not mixing yet.
Surah Ar-Rahman, among its gifts, points at exactly this: water meeting water, and something in between that holds them apart.

teach.b: Verses nineteen and twenty. Pickthall: "He hath loosed the two seas. They meet. There is a barrier between them. They encroach not." The word for barrier is barzakh.
It's a rare word, and it travels. In Surah Al-Furqan, the Qur'an pictures the same scene: one sea sweet and fresh, the other salt and bitter, with a barzakh between them.

In Surah Al-Mu'minun, barzakh names something else: the barrier behind the dead, the in-between state from death until the resurrection. So the word means a boundary that separates two things without either disappearing.

Then: from both of them come pearls and coral, and after that, the refrain: which of your Lord's favors will you deny? The two seas aren't a problem to fix. Both are gifts, and both bring up treasure.
How to picture it? Classical commentators thought of fresh rivers flowing into the salt sea, or of the seas of the earth and the sky.
In modern times, some writers connect the verse to estuaries and to layers of water with different saltiness that mix only slowly. Others caution against tying a verse to any one finding.

The Qur'an presents the two seas as a sign, something to notice, not a lab report. What everyone can take from it is the shape: two things meet, a limit holds, and each keeps what it is while both give something precious.

how: Muslims recite these verses of Ar-Rahman as signs of God's order in nature; the word barzakh is also widely known as the name for the state between death and resurrection.

games.q: two seas in Ar-Rahman — tap the pairs.

s: the verse says the two seas never meet
it says they meet, and a barrier keeps them from encroaching.
barzakh also names the state between death and resurrection
Surah Al-Mu'minun uses the same word for it.
only one of the two seas brings up treasure

games.q: the surah has just shown two seas held apart by a barrier. what comes next?
o: a warning about storms at sea.
pearls and coral come from both.
the barrier will break on the last day.
games.why: both seas give treasure, and then the refrain asks which of these favors will you deny.

practice: Close your eyes and see a wide river mouth, brown fresh water rolling out, the open sea coming in, and find the line where they meet.
Breathe in and feel the river push out; breathe out and feel the sea hold its place, neither side winning. If a relationship or a choice of yours sits on a line like that, let it rest there too.

wordCard.voice: Two seas. Surah Ar-Rahman says two seas meet with a barzakh between them, and both bring up pearls and coral. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a barrier, an in-between. Used for the line between two seas and for the state after death.

carryVoice: Your line: two seas, one barrier. Each stays itself, and both bring up pearls. See you tomorrow.
